title: A Cook's Negligence, a Hotel with No Fire Clearance, and 21 Dead in Delhi
excerpt: The Malviya Nagar fire has killed 21 people — 13 of them foreign nationals — and exposed a city-wide failure of safety enforcement in Delhi's budget hospitality sector.
body:
A devastating fire at a budget hotel in Delhi's Malviya Nagar on June 3 has killed 21 people and injured at least 28 others, making it one of the deadliest hotel blazes in the capital's recent history. The tragedy has since spiralled into a criminal investigation that now implicates the hotel's owner, its cook, and a network of alleged document fraud involving foreign nationals.

The fire broke out in the early hours of the morning at Flourish Stay Hotel in Hauz Rani. Within minutes, the multi-storey building — which operated without a fire safety clearance — was engulfed. Residents and shopkeepers were among the first to attempt rescues, pulling guests from windows before emergency services arrived.

## A Disproportionate Foreign Toll

The Ministry of External Affairs confirmed on June 5 that 13 of the 21 dead were foreign nationals: four from Nigeria, three from Kyrgyzstan, and one each from Mozambique, Liberia, Uzbekistan, Bangladesh, Congo, and Iraq. Another 20 to 22 foreign nationals were injured.

MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India is in regular contact with the respective embassies. "We are intervening with local authorities for all the paperwork that is required, as well as with the hospital authorities wherever help is required," he told reporters.

As of Saturday, 15 patients remain admitted at Max Hospital's Saket Complex, including 13 international patients. One remains on ventilator support, though five others have been successfully weaned off ventilators and are showing signs of recovery.

## The Owner Fled. The Cook Started the Fire.

Hotel owner Lavkesh Bajaj was arrested after an extensive manhunt following the blaze. He has been remanded to four days of police custody and booked under multiple sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including culpable homicide not amounting to murder, mischief by fire, and endangering life and personal safety.

Investigators allege Bajaj drove away from the scene during the chaos without assisting in rescue efforts. Witnesses told investigators that the hotel had no visible fire exits and that construction appeared unauthorised.

On Saturday, Delhi Police arrested the hotel's cook, 65-year-old Keshav Negi, after the investigation revealed the fire was allegedly caused by his negligence. Several other individuals have also been detained for questioning.

## A Deeper Scandal

The investigation has uncovered a parallel allegation: police say Bajaj allowed Bangladeshi nationals to obtain Indian identification documents using his residential address. A Police Information Report has been submitted regarding one minor connected to the case. The discovery has added a layer of document fraud to what began as a fire safety failure.

## A City-Wide Reckoning

Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has warned of strict action against officials responsible for fire safety lapses and unauthorised construction. Her office announced provisions for a maximum prison term of two years and heavy fines for guilty officials.

The fire has revived a painful pattern. Delhi has seen a series of deadly hotel and factory fires over the past decade, each followed by promises of crackdowns that fade as enforcement returns to its default state. The Flourish Stay Hotel operated in a residential area, lacked fire safety certification, and housed dozens of guests — many of them foreign visitors seeking affordable accommodation in the capital.

For the diaspora, the fire raises unsettling questions about the safety of budget hospitality in Indian cities — the very establishments that visiting relatives, students, and short-term travellers often rely on.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed distress over the incident and announced financial assistance of ₹2 lakh to the families of the deceased and ₹50,000 for the injured. But for the families of 21 people who checked into a hotel that should never have been allowed to operate, the compensation is a fraction of the accountability owed.
